pl-l4d1c2-d1e115.summary: Defines a sacrament as a sign of a sacred thing, after Augustine. 'Sacrament' also means a sacred secret, as the sacrament of the deity, so it can mean both the sacred sign and the sacred thing signified; here it is treated as a sign.
claims: A sacrament is a sign of a sacred thing.
'Sacrament' may name the sign or the sacred secret signified.

pl-l4d1c2-d1e124.summary: Gives a second definition from Augustine: a sacrament is the visible form of invisible grace.
claims: A sacrament is the visible form of invisible grace.

pl-l4d1c2.summary: Defines a sacrament with Augustine as a sign of a sacred thing. The word also means a sacred secret, as in the sacrament of the deity, so that it can name both the sacred signifier and the sacred signified, but here it is taken as a sign. A second Augustinian definition: a sacrament is the visible form of invisible grace.
claims: A sacrament is a sign of a sacred thing.
A sacrament is the visible form of invisible grace.
'Sacrament' can also mean a sacred secret.
